answer:
Run the simulation with buoyantBoussinesqPimpleFoam to model natural convection in a 2D square cavity for the de Vahl Davis benchmark at Rayleigh number Ra = 10^5.
Use a unit square cavity with side length L = 1 m and a uniform 100x100 structured mesh created with blockMesh.
Use empty boundary conditions on the front and back planes to make the case two-dimensional.
Set the left wall temperature to 300 K using fixedValue.
Set the right wall temperature to 290 K using fixedValue.
Set the top and bottom walls to zeroGradient for temperature because they are adiabatic.
Set the velocity to noSlip on all four walls.
Set gravity to (0, -9.81, 0) in the momentum equation.
Use the Boussinesq approximation for buoyancy with p_rgh as the pressure field.
Set the reference temperature TRef to 295 K.
Set the thermophysical properties to adjusted values that satisfy Ra = g*beta*(T_hot - T_cold)*L^3 / (nu*alpha) = 10^5 with L = 1 m and (T_hot - T_cold) = 10 K.
Use the adjusted property values nu = 1.5366e-3 m^2/s, alpha = 2.1643e-3 m^2/s, and beta = 3.3898e-3 1/K, which give Pr = 0.71 and Ra = 10^5.
Run the transient solver until the flow reaches steady state, for example with endTime = 1000 s and deltaT chosen so the Courant number stays below 1.
Validate the result by comparing the average Nusselt number on the hot wall against the de Vahl Davis benchmark value of approximately 4.52 for Ra = 10^5.
